name: Chatporch AI Chatbot
author: chatporch

sections.description:
Chatporch puts an AI chat button on your WordPress site. Visitors ask questions and get answers built from what you’ve told the bot about your business. When it doesn’t know, it says so and points them to your phone, email or booking link instead of making something up.

What you get

  • One-click setup. Enter your email, tick the box and click. The bot reads your site’s pages, drafts what it knows about your business and goes live.
  • Edit it inside WordPress. Change what the bot says, its colors and its starter questions from the plugin’s page. No second dashboard to log in to.
  • Answers in your words. You write who you are, what you offer and how the bot should talk. It stays inside that.
  • Lead capture. The bot can show a contact form or your booking calendar inside the chat, filled in from the conversation.
  • Every conversation saved. Read what visitors ask so you know what your site is missing.
  • Your own button. Hide the floating button and open the chat from any link or button with the [chatporch_button] shortcode or a data-chatporch-open attribute.
  • Works with AI agents and WP-CLI. An AI agent or a script can set up the bot, change what it says and read its conversations and leads. See the FAQ.

Plans

  • Free: 1 bot, 50 messages a month, no credit card.
  • Starter: $19/month, 500 messages, smarter model, no Chatporch branding.
  • Pro: $79/month, 2,500 messages.

See chatporch.com/pricing for current details.

External services

This plugin connects your site to Chatporch, the hosted service that runs the chatbot. Nothing is sent to any service until you click the setup button on the plugin’s page, or an administrator starts setup with wp chatporch connect or the chatporch/connect ability (sites that already set up a bot with version 1.0.0 keep loading the chat widget).

Chatporch (Terms of Service, Privacy Policy)

  • Setup: when you click the setup button, your server sends https://app.chatporch.com/api/v1/ your site’s address, name and tagline, the email you entered, the plugin version and a one-time code. Chatporch then requests one page of your site (/?chatporch_verify=…, user agent ChatporchVerify) to confirm you run it, and reads your home page to see whether a bot is already on it. Your server checks on the setup every few seconds until it finishes.
  • Editing: on the plugin’s admin page, your browser loads and saves the bot’s settings, conversations and leads at https://app.chatporch.com/api/v1/, using a key stored on your site. The first time, Chatporch reads your site’s pages to draft the bot’s knowledge. The wp chatporch commands and the chatporch/* abilities make the same requests from your server.
  • Removing the plugin: deleting it tells Chatporch to revoke the site’s key.
  • Existing bot: if you enter an agent name instead of connecting, your server requests https://embed.chatporch.com/v1/config with that name and your site’s address to confirm the bot may run on your domain.
  • Chat widget: once connected, each page loads the widget script from https://embed.chatporch.com/v1/chatporch.js. The visitor’s browser then fetches the bot’s settings, and when a visitor chats, sends their messages, the address of the page they’re on and their IP address (used for rate limiting) to Chatporch. Conversations are stored so you can read them on the plugin’s page. The widget keeps the open conversation in the browser’s sessionStorage, which clears when the tab closes. It sets no cookies.

Services Chatporch uses on your behalf. These don’t receive anything directly from your site; Chatporch passes them what each needs.

  • Anthropic generates the bot’s answers and drafts its knowledge from your pages. Visitor messages and your site’s page content are sent to Anthropic for that purpose. Terms, Privacy Policy.
  • Stripe handles payment when you choose a paid plan. Clicking Upgrade takes your browser to a Stripe checkout page, where you enter your card details; Chatporch sends Stripe your email and the plan. Terms, Privacy Policy.
  • Cloudinary stores and serves an image you upload for the chat button, if you upload one. The image goes to Chatporch, which stores it at Cloudinary; visitors’ browsers then load it from Cloudinary. Terms, Privacy Policy.
  • Mailgun delivers Chatporch’s emails: the welcome email after setup, approval requests, and contact requests from visitors. These emails contain your email address, your site’s address and, for contact requests, what the visitor entered. Terms, Privacy Policy.

Source code

The plugin’s admin page (assets/admin/chatporch-admin.js) is built from the Svelte source in the plugin’s admin-ui-src/ folder. It ships unminified. To rebuild it with Node 20 or later:

cd admin-ui-src/dashboard && npm ci && npm run build:wp

The output is admin-ui-src/dashboard/dist-wp/chatporch-admin.js. See admin-ui-src/README.md.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin.
  2. Click Chatporch in the admin menu.
  3. Check the email address, tick the box to agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy, and click Set up my chatbot.
  4. The chat button appears on your site. Edit the bot from the same page.

If your site already has a Chatporch bot, its owner gets an email to approve the connection first.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Chatporch account?

The plugin creates one for you with the email you enter. The free plan needs no credit card. You can also sign in at app.chatporch.com with that email to use the full dashboard.

Why did I get an approval email?

When your site already has a Chatporch bot, or your email already has a Chatporch account, the account owner approves the connection by email. This happens even when you’re the owner, so nobody can take over a bot just by installing the plugin.

Can I try it on a local or staging site?

Yes. Sites Chatporch can’t reach from the internet get a preview bot that knows your site’s name and tagline. Preview bots are deleted after 30 days. When the site goes live at its real address, connect again there and your settings carry over.

The site check failed. What now?

Chatporch confirms you run the site by requesting a page from it. If a firewall or security plugin blocks that, allow requests whose user agent contains Chatporch. If a caching plugin serves an old copy, clear the cache. Then try again.

Will it slow my site down?

The widget loads asynchronously after your page, so it doesn’t hold up rendering. It adds nothing to pages until a bot is connected.

Does it work with my theme or page builder?

Yes. The chat runs in its own isolated layer, so theme styles don’t leak into it and its styles don’t leak into your theme.

Can I open the chat from my own button?

Yes. Add [chatporch_button label="Ask us anything"] to any page, or add the data-chatporch-open attribute to any link or button. Tick Hide the floating button on the plugin’s page to remove the default one.

Can an AI agent set it up for me?

Yes. On WordPress 6.9 or later the plugin registers abilities in the chatporch category: chatporch/get-status, connect, cancel-connect, get-config, update-config, import-site-content, list-conversations, get-conversation, list-leads and set-floating-button. AI agents reach them through the MCP Adapter or the REST API (/wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/). They need an administrator account. Start with chatporch/get-status: its nextStep says what to do next.

Is there a WP-CLI command?

Yes:

  • wp chatporch connect --email=you@example.com --agree-terms sets up the bot and drafts it from your pages.
  • wp chatporch status shows where things stand and what to do next.
  • wp chatporch config get and wp chatporch config set <field> <value> read and change what the bot says.
  • wp chatporch conversations, wp chatporch leads and wp chatporch button show|hide do what their names say.

Run wp help chatporch for every option.

What happens when the bot doesn’t know an answer?

It tells the visitor and sends them to whatever you choose: your phone number, email, contact form or booking link.
sections.changelog:
1.2.0

  • AI agents can set up and edit the bot through WordPress abilities (WordPress 6.9+, e.g. with the MCP Adapter).
  • New wp chatporch WP-CLI commands for setup, settings, conversations and leads.

1.1.4

  • Turning the chatbot on or off clears the page cache of common caching plugins, so visitors see the change right away.
  • The settings screen keeps a readable width on wide monitors, and form fields are white.

1.1.3

  • When the site check fails, the plugin shows what blocked it, Cloudflare steps when Cloudflare did, and a Copy details button for emailing support.

1.1.2

  • A site whose firewall or cache blocks the check is no longer offered a 30-day preview chatbot. The fix is shown instead.

1.1.1

  • WordPress Playground sites in the browser get preview mode in one click.

1.1.0

  • Set up a bot from WordPress in one click: no visit to the Chatporch dashboard.
  • Edit the system prompt, appearance, conversations and leads on the plugin’s page, and upgrade your plan from it.
  • Preview mode for local and staging sites.
  • The plugin now has its own Chatporch menu item instead of a page under Settings.
  • Deleting the plugin revokes its connection to Chatporch.

1.0.0

  • First release.
